h: Gaming tips for a Bluewater session
p: Shopping and an action-packed game don't always mix, so a little planning helps. Drop your bags off at the car or keep them with one person, because you'll want your hands free and nothing on the floor to trip over. Trainers are a good shout too. If you've done a big shop beforehand, grab a drink before you go in; it can get surprisingly energetic in there.

Sessions run for a set time and the games on offer change, so check what's available when you book and pick something that suits your crowd. A family-friendly theme for younger players, something faster and more competitive for teens and adults. Teamwork is everything, so agree roles early: one person on targets, one on puzzles, one calling out the timer.

Bluewater opened in 1999 and has become a big name in Kent shopping, with lakes and green spaces around the outside of the centre that make for a nice break from the indoor buzz. If you fancy fresh air before heading home, there are paths around the lakes where you can stretch your legs.

Getting there is easy. Greenhithe station is close by, with buses linking it to the centre, and Ebbsfleet International, with its high-speed trains, is a short drive away. Dartford and Gravesend are both nearby too, so it's simple to combine a Bluewater trip with a visit to friends or family in north Kent.
